cards.name: Drop Shadow
cards.summary: Adds a blurred, offset copy of the object's silhouette behind it as a live effect, so the artwork looks lifted off the page. The shadow is rendered as a raster at the document's raster effects resolution; by default it is black, Multiply, 75% opacity, 7 pt right and down with a 5 pt blur.
use_for: lifting a logo or badge off a busy or light background
giving headline type depth on a poster
card / button UI mock-ups that need a soft elevation shadow
separating overlapping shapes in an infographic
avoid: Heavy, dark shadows (opac near 1, blur near 0) look dated; keep opacity 0.3-0.6 and a larger blur for a modern soft shadow.
The shadow is a raster at the Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings resolution; at screen resolution it prints soft and stepped, so set High (300 ppi) before print export.
Applied to a group it shadows the combined silhouette; applied to each object separately the shadows fall on neighbouring objects. Apply at the level you mean.

The shadow colour (sclr) is a FillStyle that the harvest's applyEffect round trip did not send, so a script is only proven for mode, offsets, blur, opacity and darkness; set a coloured shadow in the dialog or with a graphic style.
For a long flat shadow use Effect > Distort & Transform > Transform copies or a blend instead.

params.name: horz
params.does: horizontal offset of the shadow in points (positive = right)

params.name: vert
params.does: vertical offset of the shadow in points (positive = down)

params.name: blur
params.does: softness of the shadow edge in points (0 = hard-edged copy)

params.name: opac
params.does: shadow opacity stored as a fraction 0-1 (the dialog shows it as a percentage)

params.name: blnd
params.does: blend mode code of the shadow: the numbers are Illustrator's BlendModes values (harvested in the ai_blend_mode batch: 0 Normal, 1 Multiply, 2 Screen ...), not the Transparency panel order; that this key uses them is inferred from the dialog defaults (Multiply = 1 here, Screen = 2 on the glows)

params.name: csrc
params.does: colour source: a fixed colour (sclr) or the object's own colour darkened by 'dark' (mapping inferred from the dialog's Color / Darkness radio, not probed)

params.name: dark
params.does: darkness percentage used when the colour source is Darkness

params.name: sclr
params.does: shadow colour (a FillStyle; harvest default is CMYK rich black)
params.typical: black or a dark shade of the background colour

cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Drop Shadow"><Dict data="I blnd 1 I csrc 0 R horz 18 R vert 18 R blur 12 R opac 0.8 R dark 100 B pair 1 B usePSLBlur 1"/></LiveEffect>'); dialog route: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Adobe Drop Shadow"). Keys with spaces ('Adobe Effect Expand Before Version') and the FillStyle colour sclr are not part of the simple Dict string.
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect in the Appearance panel, editable or removable; Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into a raster image
cards.cost: light: one blurred raster per object, rendered at the Document Raster Effects resolution (slower at 300 ppi on large artwork)

review.changes: avoid: removed the invented '72 ppi default' Document Raster Effects claim (not in the batch; print documents start higher); coloured-shadow line now says the FillStyle colour was untested by the round trip instead of 'cannot be set'; blnd 'does' corrected: the codes are Illustrator's BlendModes values (ai_blend_mode harvest), not the blending-mode panel order, and the key mapping is marked inferred

verified.note: Every shape, the type and the zigzag carry a soft dark shadow offset down and to the right (18 / 18 pt, blur 12, 80 %), absent from ref.png, so the art looks lifted off the page as the card says.

previous.note: No frame: id absent from gallery/ai_effect/index.json and not listed in failed.json, so the render pass did not reach it.

cards.name: Feather
cards.summary: Softens the object's edges so they fade from opaque to transparent over the given radius (in points), as a live raster effect (LiveEffect 'Adobe Fuzzy Mask'). The shape keeps its colours inside but loses its crisp outline, like a vignette edge.
use_for: soft-edged photo or shape vignettes in a layout
blending a shape into a background without a hard edge
soft light spots and blobs behind headline type
fading the edge of a placed image or texture inside a design
avoid: A large radius on thin objects (hairlines, small type, the zigzag stroke) makes them nearly vanish; feather big shapes, not detail.
It is rendered as a raster at the Document Raster Effects resolution; use 300 ppi for print.
For a fade in one direction only, use a gradient opacity mask instead.
Applied to a group it feathers the group's combined silhouette, not each object.

params.name: Radius
params.does: distance in points over which the edge fades to transparent

cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Fuzzy Mask"><Dict data="R Radius 28"/></LiveEffect>'); dialog route: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Feather")
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect in the Appearance panel; Expand Appearance bakes the soft edge in as a raster soft (opacity) mask on the object
cards.cost: light: one raster soft mask per target at the Document Raster Effects resolution

review.changes: non_destructive: 'bakes it into a masked raster' contradicted the card's own cost line (a raster soft mask per target); now says the soft edge is baked in as a raster opacity mask

verified.note: Against ref every edge fades softly to transparent (box, star, circle) with interiors intact; the box outline turns to a pale rim, PGD fades to a faint ghost and the zigzag stroke vanishes, as the avoid line warns.

previous.note: Against ref every edge fades softly to transparent (box, star, circle) with interiors intact; the box outline turns to a pale grey rim, PGD fades to a faint ghost and the zigzag stroke vanishes, as the avoid line warns.

cards.name: Inner Glow
cards.summary: Adds a soft glow of colour inside the object, either along its inner edge or spreading from its centre, as a live raster effect. The harvest default is a white glow in Screen mode at 75% opacity with a 5 pt blur, which reads as a light rim just inside the outline.
use_for: glossy button and badge highlights
neon or backlit look on type and icons (with Outer Glow)
soft inner light on a flat shape to suggest volume
glowing sticker or emoji style artwork
avoid: Screen mode with a white glow does nothing on white or very light fills; switch blnd to Normal or pick a contrasting colour.
A blur larger than half the object's thickness floods thin type and strokes with the glow colour.
Rendered as a raster at the Document Raster Effects resolution; raise it for print.
Glow colour (gclr) is a FillStyle the harvest's applyEffect round trip did not send; a script is only proven for mode, type, blur and opacity, so set the colour in the dialog or with a graphic style.

params.name: gclr
params.does: glow colour (FillStyle; harvest default white)
params.typical: white or a light tint of the fill colour

params.name: gtyp
params.does: where the glow starts: from the centre or from the inner edge (see enum_labels; mapping inferred from the dialog default Edge)

params.name: blnd
params.does: blend mode code of the glow: the numbers are Illustrator's BlendModes values (harvested in the ai_blend_mode batch: 0 Normal, 1 Multiply, 2 Screen ...), not the Transparency panel order; that this key uses them is inferred from the dialog defaults (Screen = 2 here, Multiply = 1 on Drop Shadow)
params.typical: 2 (Screen) default; 0 (Normal) to show on light fills

params.name: blur
params.does: how far the glow spreads, in points

params.name: opac
params.does: glow opacity as a fraction 0-1

cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Inner Glow"><Dict data="I gtyp 1 I blnd 0 R blur 20 R opac 1"/></LiveEffect>'); dialog route: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Inner Glow"). The colour gclr is a FillStyle and is not part of the simple Dict string.
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect in the Appearance panel; Expand Appearance bakes it into a raster
cards.cost: light: one blurred raster per target at the Document Raster Effects resolution

review.changes: gclr avoid line: 'a script can set ... only' overclaimed; now says the FillStyle colour was untested by the round trip; blnd 'does' corrected: BlendModes values from the ai_blend_mode harvest, not panel order, mapping inferred

verified.note: A white glow (Normal, 20 pt, 100 %) lightens a soft rim just inside every outline (box edge 255,122,26 -> 255,165,100) while the interiors keep their colour, and the thin type and zigzag are flooded by it (type pale grey, zigzag gone), exactly as the summary and the blur avoid line say.

cards.name: Outer Glow
cards.summary: Adds a soft, unoffset halo of colour around the outside of the object as a live raster effect, the classic glow / neon halo. With the harvested mode, blur and opacity (Screen, 5 pt, 75%) and the default black colour, the harvest render shows a dark grey halo on the white artboard, which reads as a shadow ring; set a bright colour for a real glow.
use_for: neon sign type and icons on dark backgrounds
halo to separate a cut-out or logo from a busy background
glowing UI elements and game-style titles
soft backlight behind a product or badge
avoid: Screen can only lighten: over a white or light background object a light glow in Screen mode disappears, so use Normal there. On the empty artboard the glow still shows in its own colour (the harvest render of the defaults is a visible dark halo).
The harvest default colour is black, which reads as a muddy shadow ring, not a glow; pick a bright colour.
Rendered as a raster at the Document Raster Effects resolution; raise it for print.
Glow colour (sclr) is a FillStyle the harvest's applyEffect round trip did not send; a script is only proven for mode, blur and opacity, so set the colour in the dialog or with a graphic style.

params.name: sclr
params.does: glow colour (FillStyle; harvest default CMYK rich black)
params.typical: a bright saturated colour (cyan, magenta, yellow) or white

params.name: blnd
params.does: blend mode code of the glow: the numbers are Illustrator's BlendModes values (harvested in the ai_blend_mode batch: 0 Normal, 1 Multiply, 2 Screen ...), not the Transparency panel order; that this key uses them is inferred from the dialog defaults (Screen = 2 here, Multiply = 1 on Drop Shadow)
params.typical: 2 (Screen) on dark backgrounds; 0 (Normal) on light ones

params.name: blur
params.does: how far the halo spreads beyond the edge, in points

params.name: opac
params.does: glow opacity as a fraction 0-1

cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Outer Glow"><Dict data="I blnd 0 R blur 30 R opac 1 B usePSLBlur 1"/></LiveEffect>'); dialog route: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Outer Glow"). The colour sclr is a FillStyle and is not part of the simple Dict string.
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect in the Appearance panel; Expand Appearance bakes it into a raster
cards.cost: light: one blurred raster per target at the Document Raster Effects resolution

review.changes: summary and avoid: 'barely visible / invisible on white' with the Screen default contradicted the batch's render check (Effect_Stylize_Outer_Glow.png, diff 0.804: a dark grey halo, edge pixel ~166 grey, around the rectangle on the white artboard); both now describe that halo and limit the Screen warning to light background objects; sclr avoid line no longer claims the colour cannot be scripted (untested); blnd 'does' corrected: BlendModes values, not panel order, mapping inferred

verified.note: A clear cyan halo with no offset surrounds the box, circle, PGD type and zigzag (fainter but present around the blue star), absent from ref: the neon glow the card describes.

previous.note: A clear cyan halo with no offset surrounds the box, circle, PGD type and zigzag (fainter but present around the blue star), absent from ref: the neon glow the card describes.

cards.name: Round Corners
cards.summary: Rounds every corner anchor of the target paths (shapes, open strokes and type outlines) to the given radius in points, as a live vector effect; the underlying path is unchanged. The harvested default radius 0.01 pt makes no visible change, so the radius must be set.
use_for: softening a star, badge or icon set to a friendly rounded style
rounded-terminal look on outlined type for kids or food branding
taking the sharp turns out of zigzag or chart lines
consistent corner rounding across many mixed shapes at once
avoid: The radius the harvest captured (0.01 pt, the dialog's last-used value, not a factory setting) shows nothing; always set radius.
It rounds every corner equally, including type and small details; for per-corner control use live corner widgets with the Direct Selection tool.
A radius larger than a short segment collapses detail (star tips become blobs, small type loses shape).
Shapes whose corners are already smooth curves (a rounded rectangle, a circle) barely change; it only rounds corner anchors.

params.name: radius
params.does: corner radius in points applied to every corner anchor

cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Round Corners"><Dict data="R radius 45"/></LiveEffect>'); dialog route: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Adobe Round Corners")
cards.non_destructive: yes: live vector effect in the Appearance panel; Expand Appearance converts it to real rounded paths

review.changes: avoid: the 0.01 pt radius is now called the dialog's last-used value captured by the harvest (the batch evidence says defaults are last-used dialog values), not a default; the '(rx)' SVG jargon replaced with plain wording

verified.note: At radius 45 every corner anchor is rounded: the star tips become soft lobes, the PGD letters turn bubbly and the zigzag becomes a smooth wave, while the already-rounded box changes only slightly, as the card says.

cards.name: Scribble
cards.summary: Redraws fills (and, when applied to the whole object, strokes) as loose back-and-forth marker lines at a set angle, spacing and curviness, so solid art looks hand-scribbled or hatched. It is a live vector effect (LiveEffect 'Adobe Scribble Fill'); the harvest defaults match the dialog's Default setting (30 deg, 3 pt lines, 5 pt spacing, 5% curviness).
use_for: hand-drawn, sketchbook or kids' packaging look
marker-scribble highlights behind headline words
doodle-style infographics and explainer illustrations
hatched fills for a playful poster or zine
avoid: Tight Spacing with a thin StrokeWidth on large areas produces thousands of path segments: slow redraw and heavy expanded files.
On small type the scribble destroys legibility; apply it to large shapes or to a fill-only appearance.
Random variation changes when the effect is re-rendered or edited; expand the appearance to freeze a result.
For an even, mechanical hatch use a pattern fill instead.

params.name: Angle
params.does: direction of the scribble lines in degrees

params.name: StrokeWidth
params.does: thickness of the scribble line in points

params.name: Spacing
params.does: gap between neighbouring scribble passes in points

params.name: SpacingVariation
params.does: random variation of the spacing in points

params.name: Scribbliness
params.does: curviness of the turns as a fraction (dialog Curviness %): low = sharp zigzags, high = loopy

params.name: ScribbleVariation
params.does: random variation of the curviness as a fraction

params.name: EdgeOverlap
params.does: how far the lines run inside (negative) or past (positive) the path edge, in points (dialog Path Overlap)

params.name: EdgeOverlapVariation
params.does: random variation of the edge overlap in points

cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Scribble Fill"><Dict data="R Spacing 10 R Angle 45 R StrokeWidth 4 R EdgeOverlap 2 R Scribbliness 0.1 R ScribbleVariation 0.05 R SpacingVariation 1 R EdgeOverlapVariation 4"/></LiveEffect>'); dialog route: app.executeMenuCommand("Live Scribble Fill")
cards.non_destructive: yes: live vector effect in the Appearance panel; Expand Appearance converts it to stroked paths
cards.cost: moderate: vector-only, but tight spacing on large fills or type generates very many path segments

verified.note: Fills are redrawn as loose 45-degree back-and-forth marker lines in their own colours (gradient kept on the circle), the box outline and zigzag become jittery scribbled strokes and PGD is hatched, exactly the hand-scribbled look described.

previous.note: Fills are redrawn as loose 45-degree back-and-forth marker lines in their own colours (gradient kept on the circle), the box outline and zigzag become jittery scribbled strokes and PGD is hatched, exactly the hand-scribbled look described.
